questions.prompt: Compare how ethanol and ethanoic acid react with sodium hydrogencarbonate, and explain the difference.
questions.modelAnswer: Ethanoic acid reacts with sodium hydrogencarbonate, fizzing and giving off carbon dioxide, because it is an acid (it has the –COOH group that releases H⁺). Ethanol does not react because the –OH in an alcohol is not acidic enough. So the fizz identifies the acid.
